assessments.reasoning: In §3.1, printed pages 388–389, the designers say guardian processes share objects directly inside their guardian and guardians communicate through value-passed handler calls.

challenge.method: Read §3.1 through dynamic guardian creation and compared the local/global distinction in the 1987 MIT manual's remote-call discussion.
challenge.results: The 1983 text permits communicating names of guardians and handlers and excludes inter-guardian sharing of guardian-local objects. The 1987 reference separately describes the remote-call rules for global guardians, handlers, creators, and nodes. That distinction does not displace the dated design proposition.

limitations: The cited section heading is §3.1 Overview, and its subject is guardians. The review of the 1987 reference was limited to the relevant counterexample passages.
